e: A gateway VPC endpoint for DynamoDB gives private access from the VPC to DynamoDB over the AWS network, with no internet gateway or NAT, and endpoint policies add control. NAT gateways or instances and internet gateways send traffic through the internet path.

DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a fully managed, in-memory cache for DynamoDB that is API-compatible, so read-heavy workloads get microsecond reads with minimal code change and no cache management. ElastiCache requires application changes and cache logic, and global tables are for multi-Region replication.

AWS Backup centrally manages backups for EC2 and RDS and can copy them to another Region on a schedule with minimal setup. DLM doesn't handle RDS, and manual AMI/snapshot copying or exports and replication add operational work.

The EC2 instance gets permissions through an IAM role (instance profile) that allows reading the Parameter Store parameter and decrypting with the KMS key that protects it. Policies can't be assigned directly to instances, and trust relationships with RDS or Parameter Store don't grant access.

AWS WAF on API Gateway blocks web exploits like SQL injection for the API traffic, and Shield Advanced on the NLB provides detection and mitigation for large, sophisticated DDoS attacks. WAF can't be attached to an NLB, and Shield Standard and GuardDuty give less protection.

SQS decouples the microservices, buffers work, and lets consumers scale independently. Since processing order doesn't matter, a standard queue fits. SNS pushes messages without queuing for slow consumers, and Lambda or DynamoDB Streams add needless complexity.

RDS Multi-AZ synchronously replicates every transaction to a standby in another AZ, so data is on two nodes with automatic failover and minimal data loss. RDS doesn't offer three-node synchronous replication, cross-Region replicas are asynchronous, and EC2 with Lambda replication is not reliable.

S3 and CloudFront for static content, API Gateway with Lambda for dynamic content, and DynamoDB on-demand for the database remove server maintenance and scale reads and writes almost instantly. Aurora Auto Scaling scales reads but more slowly, and EC2-based designs need patching.

Configuring the Lambda function to run in the VPC (with the right security group) lets it use the VPC's routing to the on-premises data center through Direct Connect and the virtual private gateway. A separate VPN, route table edits alone, or an Elastic IP don't give Lambda access.

ECS tasks get AWS permissions via a task IAM role: create a role with S3 permissions and set it as taskRoleArn in the task definition. Security groups don't grant S3 permissions, and IAM users or editing an S3 'role' aren't the correct mechanisms.

FSx for Windows File Server provides a fully managed shared SMB file system for Windows instances across multiple AZs. EFS doesn't support Windows instances, EBS volumes can't be shared across AZs, and volume gateway presents block volumes, not a shared file system.

RDS Multi-AZ gives automatic failover for the database, and ECS on Fargate runs containers highly available with no servers to manage and automatic scaling. Read replicas don't fail over automatically by default, and EC2-based container clusters need more manual management.

AWS Transfer Family offers a fully managed, highly available SFTP endpoint that writes directly into S3, so there are no servers to run. EC2-based SFTP servers with cron jobs need management, and S3 File Gateway isn't an SFTP server.

S3 Object Lock in compliance mode makes documents immutable for the 5-year retention period, even for admins. SSE-KMS with a customer managed key supports automatic annual key rotation. Governance mode can be bypassed, and SSE-S3 doesn't let you configure rotation or imported keys rotate manually.

Elastic Beanstalk is a managed platform supporting Java and PHP with high availability, and swapping environment URLs lets the team test new features in a separate environment and switch with minimal downtime. EC2 or containers require more management, and a Lambda rewrite is a big change.

A read replica serves the reporting queries so the primary instance can process orders without timeouts, and employees can still query data. Sending orders to a replica won't work because replicas are read-only, and DynamoDB migration or scheduling are impractical.

Textract converts scanned documents to text, and Comprehend Medical extracts medical information, both run by Lambda on upload (serverless and scalable). Storing the results in S3 lets Athena run SQL queries. Rekognition isn't for document text, Transcribe Medical handles audio, and EC2 databases or custom apps add overhead.

ElastiCache for Redis caches frequent read results to reduce database reads and supports Multi-AZ replication with automatic failover for high availability. Memcached lacks replication, Route 53 caching doesn't affect database reads, and read replicas offload reads but don't reduce them as effectively.

Two EC2 instances in different AZs with a database cluster and replication gives automatic failover within the Region for high availability. A single instance with AMI backups or auto recovery has downtime, and a cross-Region setup is more complex than needed.

Sending orders to an SQS queue and having EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group consume them means orders persist and are processed automatically even after a failure; unprocessed messages remain in the queue. An ALB doesn't store requests, and the other options don't make processing durable.

DynamoDB TTL deletes expired items automatically at no extra cost. Add an attribute with the creation time plus 30 days and set it as the TTL attribute, requiring minimal development effort. The other options need custom code, instances, or stack redeployments.

Rehosting the .NET app on Elastic Beanstalk's .NET platform in a Multi-AZ deployment needs minimal code changes and is highly available, and DMS can migrate Oracle to RDS for Oracle Multi-AZ without changing the application's database engine. Lambda refactoring, Linux, or DynamoDB would require code changes.

EKS runs the existing Kubernetes workloads without changing the deployment method, Fargate removes node management, and DocumentDB is MongoDB-compatible so no code change is needed. DynamoDB would require rewriting data access, and ECS isn't Kubernetes.

Amazon Transcribe provides speaker identification (diarization) and generates transcripts, which can be stored in S3 for 7 years and queried with Athena. Rekognition is for images and video, Translate for language translation, and Textract for documents.

An API Gateway Cognito user pool authorizer validates the tokens issued to users directly, with no custom code or servers, so it's the least operational overhead. Lambda authorizers, per-user API keys, or email headers all require more development and are less secure.
